# Wave 4a brief: the words on screen (K13, review item 78)

Region: every piece of text a person reads in app.js and index.html (headings, labels, notes, toasts, empty
states, sheet copy, explanations), plus manifest.webmanifest shortcut text. Not training logic, not the evidence
cards' citations (keep their sources), not the exercise instructions' technical content (only trim their
wording if it's clearly overlong).

## The rule
On screen: a verb and a number, one line where possible. The reasons and studies go behind the existing "Why?"
chips, ⓘ buttons or a folded "More" detail, which stay one tap away. Plain words; spell out or explain RIR, RPE
and e1RM once where they first appear ("RIR: reps left in the tank"). Keep the honesty: estimates are labelled
as estimates and limits are still stated, just shorter. Keep the existing voice (direct, second person, no hype,
no exclamation marks, no emoji).

Examples to follow (from the review):
- "Part of your Together program. Together plans your heavy lifting…" (44 words) → "Your lifts and records.
  Your plan lives in Today."
- "Saved on this phone. It shapes today's plan, and over a few weeks it teaches the app…" → "30 seconds. Helps
  tune today's workout."
- "Missed some days? Starting the week again usually beats skipping ahead…" → "Missed days? Restart the week.
  You lose very little."
- "Best set each session, run through Epley with your RPE." → "Your estimated 1-rep max from your best sets."
- "2 sets fewer: quads already got hard sets earlier in the day…" → "2 fewer quad sets: squats covered them.
  [Put back]"

Targets: Today under about 150 visible words with the check-in folded; the program/customize page under about
250 visible words with details folded; no visible sentence over about 25 words outside folded details and
evidence cards. Measure visible words before and after on Today, Train, Progress (All), Library, Settings, the
customize page and each sheet, and report the numbers. Also remove leftover old names ("Hypertrophy Log",
"Strength Log") anywhere.

The browser suites assert some exact text: update those expectations to the new text (do not weaken what they
check). Everything must pass.
